correctness.rationale: Unoriented isotropic great circles admit independent chosen hemisphere normals with heights t_i uniform(0,1) and azimuths uniform. A spherical cell containing pole has small perimeter only if projected normals positively span R^2; otherwise it contains a pole-to-equator arc, forcing perimeter >=pi. On spanning (probability 1/4), gnomonic coordinates map three hemisphere inequalities EXACTLY to planar halfspaces u_i dot z >= -h_i, h_i=t_i/sqrt(1-t_i^2), a bounded triangle. For angular triple alpha_i>0 sum pi, planar perimeter is sum c_i h_i with c_i=cot(alpha_j/2)+cot(alpha_k/2). The identity product c_i^{-1}=product sin^2(alpha_i/2)/cos(alpha_i/2) is exact. For P<=epsilon, geodesic diameter <=P/2 forces each t_i<=sin(epsilon/2), giving a uniform bounded rescaled offset cube; scaled spherical perimeter tends to sum c_i s_i for fixed nondegenerate angles, and dominated convergence plus zero-measure threshold boundary gives total variation of joint angle-offset density. The 3-simplex volume is 1/(6prod c_i), and angular density is 1/(2pi^2); K=I/(12pi^2), independently numerically quadratured I=0.03667927220379739 and K=0.0003096989395690209. Transform y_i=c_i s_i; radial coordinate has Beta(3,1) and proportions Dirichlet(1,1,1), jointly independent of tilted alpha. The asymptotic all eps follows analytic domination; finite numerical integrals verify only the coefficient.
